intro: BBC Sport reports that David Sullivan is expected to be present at West Ham’s upcoming EFL Cup first-round fixture against Portsmouth on Saturday, even though he has been advised to avoid attending home matches at the London Stadium. The situation has drawn attention because it involves one of the club’s most prominent figures and a high-profile domestic cup tie.

sections.heading: What has been reported
sections.text:
According to BBC Sport, David Sullivan is likely to attend Saturday’s EFL Cup first-round match between West Ham and Portsmouth. The report adds that this is despite advice that he should not be in attendance at home games held at the London Stadium. Those are the core facts available from the source.

No further specifics about who issued the advice, the reasons behind it, or any responses from Sullivan or the club are included in the BBC Sport excerpt. The only confirmed elements from the report are Sullivan’s expected presence at the fixture, the opponent (Portsmouth), the competition (the EFL Cup first round), and the venue (the London Stadium).

sections.heading: The wider context around the people, clubs and competition
sections.text:
David Sullivan is a well-known figure in English football and is associated with West Ham United in an ownership and executive capacity. The London Stadium has been West Ham’s home ground since the club moved there, and the EFL Cup (currently sponsored under different names over the years) is a national knockout competition involving professional clubs across the English football league system.

Portsmouth are the visitors for this particular tie. Cup fixtures like this one can draw additional attention when off-field matters involve high-profile owners or executives attending matches, because appearances by senior figures often generate commentary from fans, media and club stakeholders.
